question: $p$ -Methyl benzene nitrile can be prepared from which of the following? [AP EAPCET 23 May 2024 S1]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The compound is $p$ -methylbenzonitrile, $p\text{-CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CN}$ , in which the $-\text{CN}$ group is attached directly to the aromatic ring. Such aryl nitriles are best prepared by the Sandmeyer reaction. In this route, $p$ -toluidine is first diazotized with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273\text{–}278\ \text{K}$ to form $p$ -methylbenzenediazonium chloride. The diazonium salt is then treated with $\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}$ , which replaces the diazonium group by $-\text{CN}$ and gives $p$ -methylbenzonitrile. $p\text{-CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} p\text{-CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}} p\text{-CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CN} + \text{N}_2$ The other routes do not give the required aryl nitrile: $p$ -methylbenzyl chloride with $\text{KCN}$ gives $p$ -methylphenylacetonitrile, and aryl halides do not undergo simple nucleophilic substitution with ordinary $\text{KCN}$ . Hence the correct option is the one showing diazotization of $p$ -toluidine followed by the Sandmeyer reaction (option c). © examsnet.com
